purpose: LRM 4.6.4.1: a noise function in a potential contribution is a voltage in series with the branch, not a current across it

oracle.derivation: The model is a 1k resistor written as V(p,n) <+ r*I(p,n) + white_noise(1e-18): a series source e_n = 1e-9 V/sqrt(Hz) in the out-0 branch. Vin is a small-signal short, so Rs = 1k (noisy=0) loads out to ground: onoise = e_n * Rs/(r + Rs) = 5e-10 V/sqrt(Hz), flat, at both points of lin 2 1k 2k. A host that injected the generator as a current of 1e-9 A/sqrt(Hz) between out and 0 would read e_n * (r || Rs) = 5e-7, a thousand times more.
